answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it may relay orders or receive nectar. Accounts build reputation only through signed exchanges with established peers; when a cluster of fresh identities coordinates, correlated defaults or recycled funding expose it, and the protocol burns their deposits. A sybil attacker must therefore buy and immobilize capital per identity at the wharf, while each failed identity leaves an auditable echo.
